seed_variation.verdict: Only one seed was run, so there is no seed variation to measure.
seed_variation.why: A hosted LLM cannot be seeded: our seeds only reach local random generators, and the provider's sampling (temperature etc.) is fixed for this model. So every run can give different text, and the spread across seeds measures the model's own run-to-run variation. Each seed repeats every API call. Each seed sets Python random, NumPy and torch. PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed to the FIRST seed for the whole run.

predictions.SY0103a: The team designed a voice-controlled kitchen timer with a twenty-five euro retail price and a twelve fifty production cost, agreeing to process commands on-board rather than via a phone app. They decided on a brand name wake word, a backup physical button, short voice confirmations, and multiple timers, while leaving the power source open. Nearing the end of the meeting, the project manager assigned tasks for the upcoming functional design session, including component research, cost breakdown, voice command specifications, market research on pricing and features, and wake word naming.
predictions.SY0103b: The team held a functional design meeting, reviewing device specifications while noting Tomasz was absent. They initially discussed supporting named timers and a fixed voice command set before user research led them to adopt two numbered timers with increasing alarm volumes and a twenty-five euro price tag. Moving to branding, they selected Kiko as the working name and discussed adding a two-digit display and power options, deciding to park those topics for Tomasz to review. Finally, the project manager assigned tasks regarding command lists, name testing, and market research, and agreed to email Tomasz about the timer change and chip capabilities.
predictions.SY0103c: The project manager reviewed costs and component pricing, bringing the total to eleven thirty with USB-C power. The team discussed the Kiko wake word, competitor offline positioning at twenty-five euros, and the proposed round puck design featuring a soft rubber button enclosing the display. After dropping the magnetic mount idea, the team agreed to explore color options for the next meeting and assigned tasks for the prototype model, display specs, and color options.
predictions.SY0103d: The team reviewed the updated wake word model and discussed hardware testing plans. They examined the physical prototype, decided to add rubber feet, walked through display and timer logic, and settled on two colourways, white with orange and charcoal with lime, featuring a white LED display. The team then reviewed the unit cost, calculating it at eleven forty per unit, leaving a safety margin under twelve fifty. Finally, they evaluated the product against initial requirements, confirming hands-free operation, a loud ramping alarm, and a competitive retail price point of twenty-five pounds based on its offline functionality.
predictions.SY0110a: Priya opened the kickoff meeting for the reusable coffee cup project with a deposit system, reviewing targets such as a one euro deposit, a production cost under three euros, and fifty partner cafes in the first year. The team discussed design constraints, noting that cups must survive hot industrial cafe dishwashers, fit standard takeaway lid sizes, and address potential losses. Priya assigned Tom to research durable, dishwasher-safe materials under three euros and Jonas to look into the return and deposit refund process, while Priya will ask Marta to consult cafe owners at the fair. The team concluded by scheduling their next meeting on functional design for Thursday.
predictions.SY0110b: The project manager opened the meeting by reviewing material options, selecting polypropylene, while the team discussed the return process, favoring a counter-return model over apps or return machines. The industrial designer confirmed that polypropylene stacks well and fits a ninety millimetre rim, and the team addressed financial losses from unreturned cups under the one euro deposit constraint. Next, the user interface designer proposed window stickers and cup logos for return identification, which the team welcomed. Finally, the team arranged for real-world testing at Café Lindner using commercial equipment, and concluded by recapping action items and scheduling the next meeting for the same time next week.
predictions.SY0110c: The team reviewed Tom's dishwasher test results from Café Lindner, noting that the polypropylene cups survived one hundred and forty cycles, leading them to agree on in-mould labelling and a ribbed band. They settled on a neutral slate grey base colour and established counter return rules for cracked or swapped cups. Finally, the user interface designer presented a slate grey window sticker badge, while the project manager agreed to raise the cost of lost cups with management and circulate the meeting minutes.
predictions.SY0110d: The team agreed to order ten thousand units in slate grey from the moulding company, keeping the deposit at one euro and dropping a second launch colour to maintain brand recognition. Project Manager noted the window badge design is basically final and will ask for the print file. Project Manager reviewed management's requirements, confirming dishwasher safety, lid compatibility, and a production cost of one euro fifty-four per cup. Finally, Project Manager agreed to write the final report and meeting minutes before concluding the session.

The team agreed on accessibility requirements including a lower shelf height, headphone jack, and physical help button. Finally, the team discussed barcode versus RFID options, and decided to await pricing details before making a final choice, while wrapping up with assigned tasks for the next meeting.
predictions.SY0202c: The project manager opened the meeting by reviewing the agenda, and Priya reported that RFID reader pads cost seven hundred euros per unit with ten-cent tags, leading the team to include both an RFID pad and a barcode fallback on the kiosk. Tomas presented three casing sketches, and the team selected the desk-like design with a tilted screen using oak veneer with aluminum corner strips. Hannah presented the updated user flow, explaining login, batch book scanning, renewals, and receipt options. They discussed help functions, deciding on text-to-speech for audio mode linked to Tomas's PC board choice, while keeping the fifteen-inch screen size for now and agreeing to revisit it after the mock-up.
predictions.SY0202d: The team agreed to use the licensed text-to-speech board, reviewed Hannah's screen layouts, and evaluated library services requirements. Priya gave high scores for speed, accessibility, library look, print option, and staff help, and later agreed to get tagging numbers by the end of next week. The project manager calculated the final unit cost at three thousand four hundred and ten euros, leaving enough headroom and prompting Priya to score the cost at a six. Finally, the industrial designer suggested an LED ring for the help button, which was dropped, and the team reviewed action items before wrapping up.
predictions.SY0209a: The team held a kickoff meeting for designing a protective case for the Learnly seven-inch children's educational tablet, establishing a maximum production cost of twelve fifty per case. Participants brainstormed features including screen protection, wipeable materials, carrying handles, button accessibility, and a potential name tag window. The group assigned tasks to check competitor pricing, research drop test standards, gather user feedback, ensure port accessibility, and evaluate budget-friendly materials. Finally, the project manager agreed to circulate meeting minutes and announced the next functional design meeting.
predictions.SY0209b: The project manager opened the second meeting and reviewed drop protection, selecting EVA foam. The user interface designer presented grip findings, recommending a carry handle, covered buttons, an open charging port, and a raised screen lip, while the industrial designer agreed to investigate hinge costs. The team then rejected fold-out handle stands and swappable covers, postponing standing wedges and name tags while assigning market price checks to Tomasz. Finally, Priya was asked to sketch the fixed handle and cut-outs, Ben agreed to get a supplier quote for the EVA case, and the team deferred discussing product colours to the next meeting.
predictions.SY0209c: The team reviewed survey results confirming drop protection and cleaning as top priorities, then discussed pricing and supplier quotes, noting that the eight euro forty cent per case cost leaves room in the budget. Priya presented design sketches featuring a top handle and port cut-outs, before the group agreed to incorporate a shallow wedge stand that adds sixty cents and forty grams while improving drop protection. The team agreed in principle to include a clear name tag window on the back and finalized a two-color launch palette of strong blue and lime green while dropping the idea of a stylus slot. Finally, the group reviewed the updated total cost calculation reaching ten euro thirty cents with the window included, and concluded the meeting after assigning tasks for the upcoming detailed design meeting.
predictions.SY0209d: The project manager opened the meeting by reviewing pricing figures and agreeing on the moulded foam pocket within budget. Priya presented sketches featuring a shallow tilting wedge and a landscape name tag pocket, after which Tomasz reviewed six evaluation criteria scored by the team. They rejected adding a shoulder strap and assigned toy safety and sample acquisition to Ben. Finally, the project manager reviewed all decisions, confirming the twenty-five euro price tag, and assigned final drawing and report writing tasks before concluding.
predictions.SY0304a: Hannah outlined the meeting schedule covering design phases, while Priya and Tom agreed displays should show space numbers and color-coded status. The team identified target users and discussed solar power, before debating whether to track availability using barrier counters or bay sensors. Hannah assigned Marcus to investigate sensing options, costs, and outdoor casing, while Priya agreed to survey campus users and Tom will sketch screen layouts in different sizes. Finally, the team decided to focus strictly on physical signs for now and scheduled the next meeting for the same time next week.
predictions.SY0304b: The project manager opened the functional design meeting to review findings, leading the team to agree on a large LED display, mains power from the existing barrier supply, and barrier counters with a nightly reset after dropping per-bay sensors. Marcus estimated the unit cost at around four hundred dollars, while the team discussed a potential central sign by the main gate and the project manager agreed to consult the estates office about budget and interest. Finally, the project manager assigned action items regarding mains connections, casing specifications, layout finalization, and visitor recruitment, before closing the meeting.
predictions.SY0304c: The project manager reviewed Marcus's updates regarding power supply and mounting for the car parks, noting the costly electrical run needed for the underground library. The team discussed costs per sign, confirmed the nightly reset for barrier drift, and postponed the QR code feature. Finally, the project manager assigned action items for the upcoming detailed design phase before concluding the meeting.
predictions.SY0304d: The project manager opened the detailed design meeting covering electrical costs, mounting methods, and total costs, and the marketing expert agreed to check counter drift through spot checks. The team reviewed the project evaluation against initial surveys, concluding that it met the brief despite budget constraints. Finally, they assigned remaining action items, including booking the library electrician, drafting a campus newsletter piece, and sending out reports and minutes.
